metadata.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness

problem.value: Transformers have quadratic time and memory complexity with respect to sequence length, making them slow and memory-hungry on long sequences.

evidence.quote: Transformers are slow and memory-hungry on long sequences, since the time and memory complexity of self-attention are quadratic in sequence length.

problem.value: Approximate attention methods fail to achieve wall-clock speedups because they overlook memory access overheads.

evidence.quote: One main reason is that they focus on FLOP reduction (which may not correlate with wall-clock speed) and tend to ignore overheads from memory access (IO).

contributions.value: Proposing FlashAttention, an IO-aware exact attention algorithm using tiling to reduce memory reads and writes.

evidence.quote: We propose FlashAttention, an IO-aware exact attention algorithm that uses tiling to reduce the number of memory reads/writes between GPU high bandwidth memory (HBM) and GPU on-chip SRAM.

contributions.value: Analyzing the IO complexity of FlashAttention and showing it requires fewer HBM accesses than standard attention.

evidence.quote: We analyze the IO complexity of FlashAttention, showing that it requires fewer HBM accesses than standard attention, and is optimal for a range of SRAM sizes.

contributions.value: Extending FlashAttention to block-sparse attention to create a faster approximate attention method.

evidence.quote: We also extend FlashAttention to block-sparse attention, yielding an approximate attention algorithm that is faster than any existing approximate attention method.

method_summary.value: The proposed method computes exact attention using tiling and recomputation to reduce HBM memory accesses.

evidence.quote: We apply two established techniques (tiling, recomputation) to overcome the technical challenge of computing exact attention in sub-quadratic HBM accesses.

method_summary.value: Tiling is used to split inputs into blocks, compute softmax with scaling statistics across blocks, and combine the results.

evidence.quote: The main idea is that we split the inputs Q, K, V into blocks, load them from slow HBM to fast SRAM, then compute the attention output with respect to those blocks.

method_summary.value: The method recomputes attention matrices in the backward pass using saved outputs and softmax statistics instead of storing large intermediate matrices.

evidence.quote: However, by storing the output O and the softmax normalization statistics (m, ℓ), we can recompute the attention matrix S and P easily in the backward pass from blocks of Q, K, V in SRAM.

method_summary.value: The algorithm is implemented via kernel fusion in a single CUDA kernel to avoid repeatedly reading and writing inputs and outputs to HBM.

evidence.quote: Tiling enables us to implement our algorithm in one CUDA kernel, loading input from HBM, performing all the computation steps (matrix multiply, softmax, optionally masking and dropout, matrix multiply), then write the result back to HBM (masking and dropout in Appendix B).

novelty.value: FlashAttention computes exact attention with fewer HBM reads and writes and without storing large intermediate matrices for the backward pass, yielding a memory-efficient and faster algorithm.

evidence.quote: We show how to compute exact attention with fewer HBM reads/writes and without storing large intermediate matrices for the backward pass.

novelty.value: Unlike standard gradient checkpointing that trades speed for memory, FlashAttention's recomputation speeds up the backward pass by reducing HBM accesses despite using more FLOPs.

evidence.quote: In contrast, even with more FLOPs, our recomputation speeds up the backward pass due to reduced HBM accesses (Fig. 2).

claims.value: FlashAttention achieves a 15% end-to-end wall-clock speedup on BERT-large, a 3x speedup on GPT-2, and a 2.4x speedup on long-range arena.

evidence.quote: FlashAttention trains Transformers faster than existing baselines: 15% end-to-end wall-clock speedup on BERT-large (seq. length 512) compared to the MLPerf 1.1 training speed record, 3× speedup on GPT-2 (seq. length 1K), and 2.4× speedup on long-range arena (seq. length 1K-4K).

claims.value: FlashAttention yields better perplexity on GPT-2 and higher scores on long-document classification.

evidence.quote: FlashAttention and block-sparse FlashAttention enable longer context in Transformers, yielding higher quality models (0.7 better perplexity on GPT-2 and 6.4 points of lift on long-document classification) and entirely new capabilities: the first Transformers to achieve better-than-chance performance on the Path-X challenge (seq. length 16K, 61.4% accuracy) and Path-256 (seq. length 64K, 63.1% accuracy).
